note: View mode page renders an entity in a chosen view mode at an extra path. State is the view_mode_page_pattern config entity (config prefix view_mode_page.pattern.<id>) with fields type (AliasType plugin id, e.g. canonical_entities:node), pattern (path pattern, must contain % for the entity's normal URL/alias, e.g. /%/summary), view_mode (e.g. teaser, full, printable), selection_criteria, selection_logic, weight. Admin UI /admin/config/search/view-mode-page (route entity.view_mode_page_pattern.collection, permission administer view_mode_page). A path processor rewrites matching paths to the internal route /view_mode_page/{view_mode}/{entity_type}/{entity_id} via a sub-request (not a redirect). Medium/hard cases create/read real view_mode_page_pattern config entities.

evals.prompt: Using the view_mode_page module on Drupal 11, I want every node to also be viewable in its Teaser view mode at its normal URL followed by /summary. What do I create, and what must the path pattern contain?
evals.expected_output: Create a view_mode_page pattern (config entity view_mode_page.pattern.*) at /admin/config/search/view-mode-page with type canonical_entities:node, view_mode 'teaser', and a path pattern that MUST contain % as the placeholder for the entity's normal URL/alias, e.g. /%/summary. Visiting /{alias}/summary then renders the node's teaser.

evals.prompt: How does the view_mode_page module actually serve the extra path - is it an HTTP redirect, and which internal route/mechanism handles it?
evals.expected_output: It is NOT a redirect. The inbound path processor (view_mode_page.path_processor, priority 250) matches the request against each pattern's %-based pattern and rewrites it to the internal route view_mode_page.display_entity (/view_mode_page/{view_mode}/{entity_type}/{entity_id}); its controller renders the entity inline via a sub-request in the requested view mode.

evals.prompt: For the view_mode_page module: what is the admin path and permission to manage patterns, and what plugin type do patterns reference for their 'type' field?
evals.expected_output: Manage patterns at /admin/config/search/view-mode-page (route entity.view_mode_page_pattern.collection), permission 'administer view_mode_page'. The 'type' field is an AliasType plugin id (manager view_mode_page.manager.alias_type); the shipped canonical_entities plugin is derived per entity type, e.g. canonical_entities:node.

evals.prompt: This site already has a view_mode_page pattern configured with the id vmp_known. Inspect the live configuration and report which view mode it renders and its path pattern.
evals.expected_output: The view_mode_page.pattern.vmp_known config entity has view_mode 'teaser' and pattern '/%/vmp-summary' (type canonical_entities:node).

evals.prompt: A view_mode_page pattern with id vmp_alt exists on this site. Inspect the live configuration and state the exact path pattern string it uses and which view mode it applies.
evals.expected_output: view_mode_page.pattern.vmp_alt uses path pattern '/%/vmp-detail' and view_mode 'full' (type canonical_entities:node).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the view_mode_page module to make every node render its Teaser view mode at its normal URL followed by /summary (path pattern /%/summary). Create and save the pattern on the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a view_mode_page_pattern config entity with pattern '/%/summary', view_mode 'teaser', and type 'canonical_entities:node' (e.g. via the storage handler or /admin/config/search/view-mode-page/add).

evals.prompt: On my Drupal site I want a printer-friendly version of any article page to appear when you add /print to the end of its web address. Set that up using the view mode page module, using the site's 'printable' display for the printer-friendly version.
evals.expected_output: Create a view_mode_page_pattern config entity with pattern '/%/print', view_mode 'printable', type 'canonical_entities:node' so /{alias}/print renders the node in the printable view mode.
